items.headline: Tiffany Teo wins Singapore's first gold of the 2026 Asian Games in MMA
items.summary: Singapore mixed martial artist Tiffany Teo beat Uzbekistan's Khilola Sobirova in the women's 60kg final at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on 22 September, claiming the nation's first gold of the Games on a weight tiebreak after an overtime draw. The result entitles her to S$200,000 under Singapore's Major Games Award Programme.

items.headline: Man, 22, arrested for voyeurism at an NTU campus gym
items.summary: Police arrested a 22-year-old man, confirmed by Nanyang Technological University to be a student, after a call for assistance at a hall gym on the evening of 19 September. Investigations are ongoing, and police have not disclosed what he is alleged to have done or who was affected.

items.headline: Singaporean student, 19, pleads not guilty over Johor crash that killed five
items.summary: Goh Yin Zun, 19, pleaded not guilty in a Malaysian court on 18 September to a dangerous-driving charge over a 1 June crash near Simpang Renggam that killed five people, including his 22-year-old brother and a family of four. Prosecutors allege the brothers were racing; bail was set at RM10,000.

items.headline: India coverage is unavailable in today's edition
items.summary: India's allowed domestic outlets (The Hindu, The Indian Express, Hindustan Times, The Times of India, NDTV, The Economic Times) and the fallback tier (SCMP, Al Jazeera, CNN, Bloomberg, CNBC) could not be reached with verifiable, in-window article links from the routine's environment today. Real domestic stories existed (a Supreme Court hearing on the Vande Mataram amendment and Himachal Pradesh's monsoon toll among them) but only via off-list outlets, so no India item is carried rather than link an unverified source.

items.headline: Update: UK borrowing hits GBP18.3bn in August, GBP3.5bn above the OBR forecast
items.summary: Public-sector net borrowing reached GBP18.3bn in August, the second-highest August on record and GBP3.5bn above the Office for Budget Responsibility's forecast, the ONS reported on 22 September. A record August debt-interest bill of GBP8.8bn adds to the squeeze on Chancellor John Healey before his first budget on 28 October.

items.headline: Ed Davey pitches the Lib Dems as election kingmakers with a GBP17bn tax cut
items.summary: Closing his party's conference in Brighton on 22 September, Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey pledged a GBP17bn income-tax cut, raising the higher-rate threshold to GBP56,000 and the personal allowance to GBP15,000, that he says would be funded by rejoining the EU single market and customs union. He positioned the party as potential kingmakers in a divided parliament.

items.headline: Trump tells the UN he will strike a deal or 'annihilate' Iran after the midterms
items.summary: In his UN General Assembly address on 22 September, President Donald Trump said he faces a choice between a deal with Iran, which he expects right after November's midterm elections, and moving to annihilate the Islamic Republic. He said US officials had held a roughly three-hour meeting with Iran's delegation that day, calling it very good.

items.headline: Lula uses his UN address to warn against foreign meddling in Brazil's election
items.summary: Opening the general debate on 22 September, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva said Brazil would not let domestic or foreign actors undermine its 4 October vote, declaring that Brazilian democracy belongs to Brazilians. His remarks, delivered just before Trump spoke, followed US tariffs and sanctions tied to the prosecution of former president Jair Bolsonaro.

items.headline: Erdogan calls Gaza 'the most shameful concentration camp of our time' at the UN
items.summary: In a blistering UN General Assembly speech on 22 September, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan accused Israel of a genocidal mindset and acts of state terror, and urged countries to recognise a Palestinian state. Israel's delegation, led by envoy Danny Danon, walked out while Palestinian representatives applauded.

items.headline: Update: Trump meets Zelensky at the UN as Zelensky says he is ready for a trilateral with Putin
items.summary: On the UN General Assembly sidelines on 22 September, Trump met Volodymyr Zelensky and pressed for an energy-infrastructure truce, saying Russia had lost control of its diesel industry and floating Patriot-missile production in Ukraine. Zelensky said he is ready anytime for a US-brokered trilateral with Vladimir Putin, and Trump said Putin is willing to meet.

items.headline: Qatar's emir tells the UN that Gaza 'is genocide' and the Gulf faces its most dangerous phase
items.summary: Emir Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani told the General Assembly on 22 September that restraining Israeli aggression is the true test of the international community, and urged diplomacy to end the US-Israeli war on Iran, calling the moment one of the Gulf's most dangerous phases.

items.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Sol and Luna, halving token prices
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and Luna on 22 September at half the price of the 5.6 series, Sol at $2 and $10 per million input and output tokens, Luna at $0.10 and $0.50, and says Sol makes about half as many mistakes as its predecessor while running far cheaper.

items.headline: Alibaba unveils the Zhenwu V900 AI chip and a 20GW data-centre goal
items.summary: At its Apsara Conference in Hangzhou on 22 September, Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu introduced the Zhenwu V900 accelerator, three times the performance of its prior chip and able to link clusters of up to 500,000 cards, with mass production targeted for the first quarter of 2027, and pledged to exceed 20 gigawatts of data-centre capacity by 2032. Hong Kong shares rose as much as 5.1%.

items.headline: FAA begins an $875M AI air-traffic rollout at Washington-area airports
items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration started limited deployment on 21 September of SMART, an $875 million AI system that predicts congestion to cut delays, first around three Washington DC-area airports ahead of a planned nationwide rollout. The controllers' union NATCA said it was not involved in the system's design or testing.

items.headline: SoftBank seeks over $11 billion in junk bonds to fund its OpenAI bet
items.summary: SoftBank is marketing more than $11 billion in dollar- and euro-denominated high-yield bonds, expected to price around 24 September, to help fund a $30 billion follow-on investment that would lift its stake in OpenAI to about 13%. It is already 2026's largest junk-rated borrower.

items.headline: Update: Oil falls a fifth straight day as US-Iran talks ease supply fears
items.summary: Brent crude fell about 1% to settle at $99.25 a barrel on 22 September and WTI shed 1.2% to $94.59, the longest losing streak for both benchmarks in over a year, after Trump said US officials met Iran's delegation for three hours at the UN and Saudi Arabia moved to restart its East-West pipeline.

items.headline: Wall Street holds just shy of records as the AI rally pauses
items.summary: US stocks were little changed on 22 September, with the S&P 500 up about 0.2% to finish within 0.2% of its all-time high and the Dow slipping around 185 points, as a blistering run in AI-linked shares steadied a day after Monday's sharp gains.

items.headline: Bitcoin leads crypto back above $3 trillion as leveraged bets build
items.summary: Digital assets reclaimed a combined $3 trillion in value for the first time since January on 22 September, with Bitcoin trading around $86,600, though a surge in leveraged perpetual-futures positioning raised the risk of sharp reversals.

items.headline: US Treasury yields hold near 4.95% as investors await fresh Fed signals
items.summary: The 10-year US Treasury yield held around 4.95% on 22 September, having dipped back under 5% earlier in the week, with the two-year near 4.74%, as traders awaited data and Federal Reserve commentary for the next policy cue.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli leads by 81 as F1 heads to a Saturday showdown in Baku
items.summary: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli (292 points) begins a run of races 81 points clear of Mercedes team-mate George Russell (211) at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, Round 15, whose race has moved to Saturday 26 September for Azerbaijan's Remembrance Day. Antonelli cannot clinch the title in Baku; the earliest opportunity is Singapore.

items.headline: 🏏 Update: India crush Sri Lanka by 147 runs to retain Asian Games women's cricket gold
items.summary: India posted 216 for 3, Smriti Mandhana 79 off 45 balls with seven sixes and Richa Ghosh 49 not out off 22, then bowled Sri Lanka out for 69 to win the Aichi-Nagoya final by 147 runs on 22 September, a second successive Asian Games gold after Hangzhou 2023.

items.headline: 🏏 Will Jacks stars with bat and ball as England beat Sri Lanka by 89 runs
items.summary: At Chester-le-Street on 22 September, Will Jacks made 46 not out and then took a maiden ODI five-for (5 for 22 in seven overs), and Harry Brook top-scored with 67, as England's 265 proved plenty and Sri Lanka were bowled out for 176 to trail the series 1-0.

items.headline: 🎾 Alcaraz and Zverev headline Team Europe at the London Laver Cup
items.summary: The 2026 Laver Cup runs 25-27 September at The O2 in London, with Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev leading Yannick Noah's Team Europe against Andre Agassi's Team World, which features Taylor Fritz and Alex de Minaur, across nine singles and three doubles matches.

items.headline: Hubble and Webb team up to find 27 tiny, far-flung solar-system objects
items.summary: Using NASA's Hubble and James Webb telescopes together for the first time on such distant bodies, astronomers detected 27 small trans-Neptunian objects, some of the smallest and faintest ever directly seen, and unexpectedly found fewer small bodies than formation models predict. Two papers appeared in The Astronomical Journal.

items.headline: ESA's Juice probe swings past Earth for a Jupiter-bound gravity assist
items.summary: The European Space Agency's Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer will pass within 8,640 km of Earth on 28 September, a flyby that deflects its path by about 20 degrees and adds roughly 3.5 km/s of speed. Its ten instruments are switched on from 23 September to 3 October, and it is due to reach Jupiter in July 2031.

items.headline: Accelerated biological ageing may help explain rising early-onset cancers
items.summary: Analysing more than 150,000 young adults in the UK Biobank, researchers found biological ageing (measured by PhenoAge) has risen across birth cohorts, about 23% higher for those born 1965-1974 than 1950-1954, and is linked to greater risk of early-onset solid cancers, driven by lung, gastrointestinal and uterine cases. The work appeared in Nature Medicine.

fun_fact.headline: You are taller in the morning than at night
fun_fact.body: You are measurably taller in the morning than at night. Over the course of a day, gravity gently compresses the soft, fluid-filled discs between your spine's vertebrae, so most adults lose roughly 1 to 2 cm of height by evening and regain it overnight while lying flat. The effect is so real that astronauts, freed from gravity in orbit, can grow up to about 3 percent taller during a long stay in space.

puzzle.title: The Tumbling Die
puzzle.body: A standard die rests on a table, opposite faces summing to 7. Right now: 1 is on top, 2 faces you (south), 3 faces east (your right). Without lifting it, tip the die over its east edge twice, then over its north edge once. Which number is on top now?
puzzle.approach: Track just the top face as the die rolls; opposite faces always sum to 7.
puzzle.answer: 2. Rolling east cycles top->east->bottom->west->top (north/south fixed). After two east rolls the top is 6 with south still 2; rolling north brings the old south face (2) to the top.

word_puzzle.title: Around the Box
word_puzzle.body: Letter Boxed with 3 letters per side. TOP: C B R; RIGHT: L S K; BOTTOM: I P E; LEFT: M A D. Build words of 3+ letters; consecutive letters must come from different sides; each new word starts with the previous word's last letter; use all 12 letters in two words.
word_puzzle.approach: Chain two words that together use all 12 letters; the second word must start with the last letter of the first.
word_puzzle.answer: CLIMBS -> SPARKED (C-L-I-M-B-S then S-P-A-R-K-E-D); no two consecutive letters share a side and all 12 letters are used.
